title: Study of the Anomalous Hall effect by tuning the spin orientation in the Altermagnetic material CrSb
authors: Sreedevi Chintalapudi, Upasana Agrawal, Suvadip Das
abstract: Recent development in the field of altermagnetism, and increased demand for the search of applications of anomalous hall effect have ushered in a new era for novel quantum phases in materials. Quantum materials previously anticipated to be scientifically predictable have unfolded novel properties that brought them into the spotlight. These manifestations have led us to rethink our understanding of existing classification of magnetic materials and preexisting notions about anomalous hall effect in the light of topologically nontrivial phases of matter. One such recent de- velopment lies in the novel class of alter-magnetic materials with prospect for quantum computing. In this article, we delineate the spin and orbital resolved electronic spectrum, mode-decomposed phonon dispersion relations, geometrical berry curvature and topological surface states and their implications on anomalous Hall conductivity in the promising altermagnetic compound CrSb. We further utilize first principles calculations coupled with computationally efficient maximally localized wannier states of numerous magnetic configurations of the altermagnet to simulate the effect of external fields and elucidate the fact that the linear behaviour of anomalous hall conductivity with magnetization does not necessarily hold true for all magnetic classes, such as altermagnets.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates the Anomalous Hall effect in the altermagnetic material CrSb. Using advanced DFT calculations, the authors map out the electronic structure and topological properties of the material under various spin alignments. The key finding is that the AHE conductivity does not follow a simple linear relationship with magnetization for altermagnets, suggesting a necessary revision of current theoretical models.
main_problem: The study investigates the Anomalous Hall effect (AHE) in the altermagnetic material CrSb, specifically questioning the conventional assumption that AHE conductivity must scale linearly with magnetization.
main_result: The authors demonstrate through calculations that the anomalous Hall conductivity in altermagnets like CrSb does not necessarily exhibit a simple linear dependence on magnetization, challenging existing theoretical frameworks for magnetic materials.
method: The research employs first-principles Density Functional Theory (DFT) coupled with maximally localized Wannier functions to calculate electronic spectra, Berry curvature, and topological surface states.
model_or_system: The physical system is the altermagnetic compound CrSb. The theoretical framework involves calculating the AHE using Kubo formalism and analyzing the dependence of the anomalous Hall conductivity on various spin configurations and external fields.
key_observables: Anomalous Hall conductivity (sigma_xy), electronic band structure, phonon dispersion relations, geometrical Berry curvature, and topological surface states.
important_parameters: The analysis considers multiple magnetic configurations (e.g., coplanar vs. staggered spin orientations) and the dependence on the net magnetic moment.
main_assumptions: The study assumes that standard AHE models based on simple linear magnetization scaling are insufficient for describing complex magnetic orders like altermagnetism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate band structures for different spin orientations, phonon dispersion relations, and crucially, show the calculated anomalous Hall conductivity dependence on various sublattice spin alignments, confirming non-linear behavior.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the theoretical background of AHE in novel magnetic phases (altermagnetism), detailing advanced computational methods using MLWF/DFT, presenting calculations for CrSb's electronic and topological properties, and concluding with a re-evaluation of the linear magnetization dependence theory.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the rigorous calculation of topological invariants (Berry curvature) and their relation to transport coefficients provides advanced theoretical tools applicable to understanding quantum response in strongly correlated systems.
